header: L15 · The ground that moves · sonnet
verdict: Mostly yes: the tested window, the upstream decoding rule, the re-probe table and the fail-closed I22 are in the text and match their resolutions. The largest remaining gap is that the new probe-staleness checks of 11 11.3 and 11 11.4 cannot be implemented as written (host.upstream does not carry the pins the table names; acceptance demands every block A result sit at the floor, which a widened window contradicts), and three error-id and unknown-field rules overlap or contradict 03.

findings.defect: The `host.upstream` rule says it records 'the frontend pin for A11 to A13, the agent version for C3 and C5', but the 11.4 table lists the workload digest for A12/A15/C3/C5, herdr for A13 and mise for C2/B4. A12 reads the workload and A13 herdr, not the frontend; nothing records the workload digest, herdr pin or mise pin a result was measured with.
findings.scenario: T020 implements 'tools/ci probes fails when a block A result of a probe the table lists records an upstream version or digest other than its current pin'. A workload bump changes the digest, A12 and A15 results carry no digest, so the check can never fire and the bump merges without the re-probe the table promises.
findings.change: Define host.upstream as a map keyed by pin (frontend, workload, herdr, mise, agent), filled by the harness for every probe that the 11.4 table lists under that pin, and make the check compare each key to the pin file. Fix the 'A11 to A13' sentence.

findings.defect: 11.4 makes `tools/ci acceptance` fail when any block A result's `sbxVersion` differs from the floor, while 10.3 widens the tested window by re-recording only A4, A5 and A9 at a newer sbx without raising the floor. One result file per probe per host means those three results then carry a version other than the floor.
findings.scenario: A new sbx minor is added to the window: A4, A5 and A9 are re-recorded at it, acceptance reads sbxVersion != floor and fails on every later release, or the maintainer must raise the floor, which the window rule says it need not. The two rules cannot both hold.
findings.change: State what acceptance compares: every block A result's sbxVersion is a member of the tested window (and the newest result set equals the newest recorded version), or name the probes that must stay at the floor. Say how results for two sbx versions coexist on disk.

findings.defect: Three error ids cover the same event, an upstream output of an unexpected shape: `upstream-shape` (RJ-310, every decoder), `sbx-output-unparsed` (RJ-309, 'one that lacks a field' in 10.3 and gate 1) and `lock-unparsed` (RJ-325). 03 says a missing or mistyped field is `upstream-shape`; 10.3 says the same for sbx is `sbx-output-unparsed`. The 4.4 table gives no precedence rule.
findings.scenario: A fixture drops a field of `sbx ls --json`. One test asserts RJ-310, the doctor test of I22 asserts RJ-309; tests assert ids, never text, so both cannot be written from the spec. The same for a mise.lock missing field (RJ-310 or RJ-325).
findings.change: Pick one rule: `upstream-shape` is the id of a missing or mistyped field of any upstream; `sbx-output-unparsed` and `lock-unparsed` are only for a body that does not parse at all, or are retired in favor of upstream-shape with the upstream name in the details. Say it in the 4.4 rows.

findings.defect: 03 lists `mise.lock` among the upstream outputs decoded tolerantly ('unknown fields are allowed'), and 07 7.5 step 1 makes 'a lock with an unknown top-level key' a sync error.
findings.scenario: The pinned mise writes a new informational top-level key in a patch release. Under 03 the lock decodes; under 07 every sync of every repo with that lock exits 2 `lock-unparsed`, with the fix 'relock', which regenerates the same key. The parser author has two opposed rules for one decoder.
findings.change: Decide which side holds and say so in both places. If unknown top-level keys must fail because the lock drives egress derivation, exempt mise.lock from the 'unknown fields are allowed' sentence in 03 and give the reason; otherwise drop the clause from 07.

findings.defect: T020 (implements 11 11.4) lists no acceptance row for the new checks: a result whose recorded upstream differs from its current pin, a guide page naming a probe id its `affects` does not list, and an A5 result outside the tested window.
findings.scenario: The task is accepted with only the old rows, and the staleness rules the round added are implemented late or not at all; the spec and the plan disagree.
findings.change: Add one fixture row per new check to T020 and to the task that makes acceptance compare sbxVersion with the window.

findings.defect: `agent-path-missing` makes a salvage incomplete for any profile path that does not exist, but a sandbox whose agent never created a todos or scratch directory legitimately lacks it; the text cannot tell drift from never-created.
findings.scenario: `romeu recreate` on a freshly used sandbox exits 5 with agent-path-missing and the operator must pass --accept-loss for a path that never existed; the flag becomes routine and hides a real move.
findings.change: Split the profile paths into those that must exist at the pinned agent (checked by setup and by probe C3/C5) and optional ones; only a missing required path is a skipped item.

findings.defect: The resolution said to date the 'documented sbx behavior' with an sbx version and a doc date and to name A3 as the probe that re-confirms it. The text names the sbx version only through probe A1 and gives no doc date.
findings.scenario: A reader cannot tell when the claim 'additional workspaces are direct mounts' was last read from the docs, so a later sbx doc change goes unnoticed until A3 runs.
findings.change: Add the doc date (or the documentation page and the version it described) next to the sentence in 2.6.

pages_read: docs/reviews/lenses.md (L15, What a reviewer returns, How stage A runs)
out_of_scope: ADR 0007's mise counterpart sentence (L15-23, M: goes to the operator batch) and the round-8 findings marked L (L15-8, L15-10) or parked (L15-24, L15-25) were not re-reported. L15-21 moved with the deferred tool of 12.10. Pages 00, 13 and the other ADRs were skimmed only. Whether the claimed sbx and mise behavior is true at the pinned versions cannot be settled from text.
confidence: Medium-high on the four Required findings, each read directly in the cited lines; medium on the two Advisory ones.
